transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for fitting me in, I really appreciate it. 

Um, I hope I can explain this right... I guess I came in because I've been having a little bit of trouble at work lately. I'm a jeweler, and... well, it's a bit embarrassing, honestly. When people ask me a very simple question, like just asking when a ring repair will be ready to pick up, my answer just sort of... gets away from me? Like, I'll start explaining about the invoices, and then somehow that reminds me of garden soil, and then suddenly I'm talking about my mortgage papers. 

I can see them looking at me, and I know I'm completely losing them. I just... I don't want to make my customers uncomfortable or seem unprofessional, you know? Does that make sense? I'm hoping it's just a little stress or something you can help me fix.
Do you ever feel like you are seeing, hearing, or sensing things that other people around you cannot perceive?

Oh, um... well... I mean, nothing frightening or anything like that. I want to be completely honest with you, but I hope this doesn't make me sound... well, crazy. It's probably just because I work alone a lot, you know? 

But... sometimes, when the shop is really quiet, I'll hear a woman sort of mutter my name from back in the polishing room. Or... I'll suddenly smell burning metal, even when I know for a fact all the torches are completely off. It always feels real enough that I actually get up and go check, just to be safe. 

But it's probably just an old building being drafty, or maybe my mind just playing tricks on me because I'm a little tired. That's fairly normal when people are stressed, right? I'm sure it's nothing to really worry about... is it?
Have you noticed any recent changes in your physical health, such as memory problems, headaches, or difficulty with your vision or coordination?

Oh, no, actually... I think I'm doing really well in that department. My physical health has been perfectly fine, thankfully. I haven't had any bad headaches, and my vision is still sharp—which is so important for the tiny clasps and stones I work with, you know? 

And my coordination is just fine. My hands are still very steady. As for memory... well, I remember things okay, I just... get a little tangled up when I'm explaining things sometimes, like I mentioned before. But physically, everything is completely normal. 

I hope that's a good sign? I really try to take good care of myself, so I'm glad I can at least give you a good answer for that one. Am I giving you the right kind of information? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
When you are speaking to others, do you ever find that your thoughts become so jumbled or disconnected that you are unable to finish a sentence or express a coherent idea?

Um, yes... I think that's actually exactly what I was trying to say earlier. I hope I didn't explain it poorly the first time. 

It's just that... well, like I was saying, if a customer asks something so simple, like when their ring repair will be ready, I want to give them a good answer. But then my mind just sort of... skips around. I'll start talking about the repair invoices, and then somehow that makes me think of the garden soil I need to buy, and before I know it, I'm talking to them about my mortgage papers. 

I can see in their eyes that they're completely lost, and I just... I can't seem to pull the sentence back to where it started. It's not all the time, though! Just... enough that it's a little embarrassing. I really hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is. Does that make sense, the way I'm describing it?
How long have you been experiencing these episodes of jumbled speech and hearing or smelling things that aren't there?

Oh, um... let me think, I want to make sure I give you the right timeline. I think... well, the hearing my name, and those odd smells... and also, I guess sometimes I get a little overly worried that customers are watching us in the shop, which I know sounds silly... but all of that started around a year and eight months ago. Give or take a little bit. 

I really hope it's okay that I waited this long to bring it up. I just kept thinking it was normal stress and I didn't want to be a bother to anyone. Is that a helpful timeline for you? I hope I haven't made things harder for you to figure out by trying to just push through it for so long.
Are these moments where your thoughts become tangled and your speech shifts to unrelated topics happening almost every day, or do they happen only occasionally?

Well, um... I guess it happens more often than I'd like to admit. It's not every single day, I don't think... but it's enough that it's becoming a little bit of a problem at the shop. 

Like I was saying, it's just so embarrassing when a customer asks a perfectly normal question, like when their ring repair will be ready, and I just... I start out fine, but then my brain sort of hops from the invoices, to the garden soil I need, and then suddenly I'm talking about my mortgage papers. And I can just see them losing me, you know? They get this polite but confused look on their face. 

I really try to catch myself and steer it back, I promise I do. I don't want to make it sound like I'm completely incapable of having a conversation. It's just... those moments happen frequently enough that it made me think I should finally come in and talk to someone. I hope that's the kind of detail you were looking for? I'm trying my best to be accurate for you.

When you are speaking to customers and your thoughts become jumbled, do you find that your facial expressions or your tone of voice seem to match what you are talking about, or do you feel like your emotions are somewhat 'flat' or perhaps not matching the situation at all?

Um... I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I always try to be polite and cheerful with the customers, you know? A good attitude is so important in a jewelry shop. 

I hope I'm not giving you the wrong impression, but I don't think I've ever felt like my emotions were flat or... or not matching what's happening. I try very hard to be present and warm with people. I'm so sorry if that's not a very helpful answer. Does that make sense, or did I misunderstand the question? I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Aside from the moments where your speech gets tangled, have you ever felt that your behavior or your way of moving and acting has become strange, unpredictable, or completely out of character?

Oh, um... no, I really don't think so. I try so hard to just keep things normal and steady, you know? I haven't noticed myself doing anything unpredictable or... or strange like that. 

I always want to make sure I'm acting appropriately, especially since I handle such delicate pieces at work and I really need to be reliable for the customers. I just try to go about my day as quietly and normally as I can. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have anything like that to report. I always worry a little that I'm wasting your time when I keep saying no to the things you're asking about, but I promise I'm just trying to be as honest as possible. Am I doing okay with answering these questions for you?

Since you mentioned that these difficulties with your speech and the experiences of hearing or smelling things started about twenty months ago, have these issues consistently interfered with your ability to perform your job or maintain your social relationships throughout that entire period?

Oh, um... well, I really don't want to make it sound like I'm failing at my job or anything. I still go in every day and try to do my absolute best. But... I suppose, if I'm being completely honest, it has made things a little tricky over the last year and a half or so. 

I've actually, um... I've had to cut back just a tiny bit on the custom pieces. It's mostly just because I was starting to miss a few repair deadlines, which is so unlike me, and... well, like I mentioned before, I can sort of lose track of things during the client consultations. I really hate letting anyone down, so I thought it was safer to take on a little less. 

And, um, my husband has been so incredibly sweet about everything. He actually comes in and double-checks the invoices for me now. I used to handle all of that myself, completely fine, but it's just... it's nice to have a second pair of eyes right now, just to make sure the customers are being billed right. I hope that doesn't make me sound terribly incompetent? I'm still doing a lot of the work, I promise. Is it okay that I'm getting a little help from him like that? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing.

During these past twenty months, have there ever been any periods where these experiences—like hearing your name or the disorganized way of speaking—became much more intense or frequent, lasting for at least a month?

Well, um... I guess they've been pretty steady for the most part. I mean, the whole thing—hearing my name, those strange smells, and, um, worrying so much about the customers watching us... it all started about a year and eight months ago, like I said. 

I try really hard not to let it get out of hand, you know? I don't want to be a bother to anyone, especially at work. There might have been times when it felt a tiny bit more noticeable, but I always just try to push through and keep a smile on my face. I really don't think there was a whole month where it was terribly intense... or at least, I hope it wasn't. I just try to manage it quietly. 

Does that answer your question? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline. I'm trying my best to remember exactly how it's been.
